# ChartBook

> A developer platform for data science teams to discover, document, and share analytics work. Provides a centralized catalog for pipelines, charts, and dataframes with automatic documentation website generation.

ChartBook organizes analytics work into **pipelines** (self-contained projects) or **catalogs** (multi-pipeline collections). All configuration uses TOML format (`chartbook.toml`).

## Quick Start

- [Getting Started](getting-started.html): `pip install chartbook` — one install, everything included
- [Vocabulary](guide/vocabulary.html): the words, defined once. A manifest asks, a lockfile records what was got, a snapshot records what was made, an index records what a site shows; repository → index → pages → site; a writer per site tool
- [CLI Reference](reference/cli.html): `chartbook init`, `chartbook docs build`, `chartbook run`, `chartbook run`, `chartbook snapshot`, `chartbook restore`, `chartbook lineage`, `chartbook pin`, `chartbook update`, `chartbook docs open`, `chartbook check`, `chartbook trust`, `chartbook path`, `chartbook publish`, `chartbook catalog`, `chartbook ls`, `chartbook data`, `chartbook store`, `chartbook config`, `chartbook install claude-skill`

## Guides

- [Documenting a Pipeline](guide/documenting-a-pipeline.html): Describe charts, dataframes, notebooks, notes, models and files in `chartbook.toml`; `[files]` for files that are not tables (archives, text, PDFs, images, arrays)
- [Depending on Another Pipeline](guide/depending-on-pipelines.html): snapshots, pins and the lockfile; `chartbook run --snapshot` (them), `chartbook pin` / `update` (you); never read another pipeline's folder; `--frozen` in CI; model versions and labels
- [Keeping Costly Outputs](guide/keeping-costly-outputs.html): `keep = true` on an output that cost money or compute (a paid API run's output, a trained model): every version stays in the store, `chartbook restore` puts it back, `chartbook run` stops before remaking it (`--remake`); the doit recipe
- [Catalogs and Data Access](guide/catalogs-and-data.html): Aggregate pipelines; load any cataloged dataset with `data.load()`; every snapshot of every pipeline is its own site under `versions/`, listed on the catalog's Versions page; a `[pipelines]` entry with no path shows a pipeline from the store alone
- [Reading From a Databricks Warehouse](guide/reading-a-warehouse.html) (experimental): `[sources.x] backend = "databricks"` after `pip install chartbook[databricks]`; `DATABRICKS_HOST` + `DATABRICKS_TOKEN`; a token goes only to the host the machine names; lazy reads; a Databricks Free Edition walk-through
- [Plotting](guide/plotting.html): One call produces interactive HTML plus static PNG/PDF
- [Writing a Plotting Backend](guide/plotting-backends.html): The `PlottingBackend` contract, the `chartbook_plotting` entry-point group, and a complete example
- [How the Build Works](guide/how-the-build-works.html): resolve (the index) → write (a writer: pages from the index and the files it names; Sphinx by default, MkDocs with `[project] writer = "mkdocs"` and `pip install chartbook[mkdocs]`) → build (the site tool); incremental builds (Sphinx); template overrides in the project root

- [Roadmap](roadmap.html): what works now (one machine, a store in a shared or synced folder), what is experimental (Databricks), what is next (Delta pins, Snowflake, other warehouses, a database as the store, an MCP server)

## Reference

- [Configuration](reference/configuration.html): Complete `chartbook.toml` reference with all fields, types, and defaults
- [Python API](reference/api.html): `from chartbook import data; lf = data.load(pipeline="my_pipeline", dataframe="df_id")` — pipeline accepts a bare name or a scoped name (`myorg/my_pipeline`)

## Key Commands

```bash
chartbook init            # Scaffold a new pipeline project
chartbook init --github   # ...then git init, commit, create a private GitHub repo with gh, and push
chartbook docs build      # Render the HTML documentation website (was `chartbook docs`)
chartbook run           # Make everything current: run [scripts] build, then render the site
chartbook docs build -f   # Force overwrite existing docs
chartbook docs build -f --watch  # Rebuild incrementally on every file change
chartbook docs open          # Open the generated site (was `chartbook browse`)
chartbook check              # CI gate: missing metadata, broken paths, dependencies that cannot be found, expiring licenses
# every build also writes docs/index.json: a record per pipeline, dataframe, column, chart,
# notebook, note, model and files asset, each with an ID (scope/pipeline:kind/name) and a content hash,
# and docs/llms.txt: a line per pipeline, dataframe, chart, model and files asset with its ID and page link
# (a catalog's also links each version's own llms.txt); read it first to find your way around a site
chartbook path <name>        # Print the path chartbook.toml declares for a dataframe
chartbook path chart/<name>  # ...for a chart (also notebook/<name>, note/<name>, model/<name>, file/<name>)
chartbook path file/<name> --files  # the asset's files, one per line, sorted: a folder's files, a glob's matches
chartbook path <pipeline>:<name>  # another pipeline's asset: the pinned copy in the store (a first read pins it)
chartbook path model/<name>@<version>  # a version of a model: by the start of its hash, or by a label from [models.<name>.aliases]
chartbook path <dep>:model/<name>@champion  # another pipeline's labelled version, as pinned in chartbook.lock (pin reads labels from the snapshot; update moves them)
chartbook index diff BEFORE AFTER [--json] [--exit-code]  # what changed between two builds, from their index.json: data, pins, versions, labels, staleness
# A model is out of date when what it was trained on has moved: its page says so, index.json has stale_inputs, `chartbook check` warns; `chartbook run` retrains
# In Python: data.sql("select * from {df_a} join {df_b} using (date)") runs SQL with dataframes named in braces (DuckDB, or the warehouse of a databricks source);
# data.ref("df") is a dataframe's name in SQL; data.connect("source") the raw connection. [sources] in chartbook.toml.
chartbook publish            # Stage publishable files to a directory
chartbook create-data-glimpses  # Create data summary report
chartbook run --snapshot     # Build, then declare the build ready for others (a snapshot); checks everything is committed first
chartbook snapshot           # The second half alone: this pipeline's built assets into the store, labelled with the commit; refuses unless its pins account for every dependency
chartbook restore [name...]  # The mirror of snapshot: this pipeline's assets back on disk from its snapshots; with no names, every `keep = true` asset that is missing; never over a file
chartbook lineage            # Every snapshot upstream, walked through the pins and checked by hash; --check exits 1 on a gap, --rehash re-hashes the bytes, --json; `chartbook snapshot --deep` refuses on an upstream gap
chartbook add acme/rates     # Declare a dependency by its ID ("acme/rates" = {}) and pin its newest snapshot from the store, no folder or clone; --as NAME, --commit C
chartbook pin                # Freeze what [dependencies] have: each one's newest snapshot, into chartbook.lock
chartbook pin --frozen       # Write nothing but the store's note for gc; exit 1 unless the lockfile is complete and every pin is in the store (CI, read-only shared store: a folder, or s3://bucket/prefix with chartbook[s3])
chartbook update [dep...]    # Move pins forward to each dependency's newest snapshot
chartbook run [script]       # Run a [scripts] entry here (default: build, after pinning what has no pin); never builds in a folder it depends on, but --upstream builds and snapshots one with no snapshot
chartbook run --frozen       # Pin nothing, fetch nothing, write nothing but the store's note for gc; build only if every pin is in the store
chartbook run --remake       # Build even though a `keep = true` asset is missing while the store has it; without it, run and build stop and say `chartbook restore`
chartbook trust              # Say this folder's pipeline is yours to build (at a terminal the first build asks: y trusts, r renders without its code, Enter stops); until then a build of it runs as a build of files from a store (--render, --repository, --list, --forget)
chartbook store info         # Which store this machine uses, what set it, and the cache folder
chartbook store verify       # Re-hash everything in the store; exit 1 if an object changed
chartbook store gc           # Remove old snapshots and what nothing names (asks first; --keep-days, default 7; --keep-lineage keeps every snapshot upstream of a kept one; --aggressive lets tags, branches and labels keep nothing; every version of a `keep = true` asset stays)
chartbook store migrate      # Move a store made by ChartBook 0.2 to 0.3's layout (a folder per pipeline, a folder per snapshot, each file once); once, after every machine has 0.3; --dry-run first
chartbook store export ID --to DIR   # One pipeline's snapshots into DIR/pipelines/<pipeline>/, to send (--latest, --snapshot COMMIT[@MADE_AT])
chartbook store import DIR    # Copy the snapshots in DIR (an export, or a pipeline's folder) into this store, each file checked against its record
chartbook config             # Configure default catalog path
chartbook install claude-skill  # The Claude Code skill, user-level (--project: ./.claude/skills/chartbook); its SKILL.md names the ChartBook it is for
chartbook catalog init       # Create the global catalog, ~/.chartbook/chartbook.toml
chartbook store add NAME URL  # Add a store; a pipeline enters by snapshot
chartbook catalog disable <id>  # Leave a pipeline out of the catalog's builds; `chartbook catalog enable <id>` brings it back
chartbook catalog build   # Render the catalog site (was `catalog build`)
chartbook catalog open       # Open the catalog site in the browser
chartbook ls                 # List all pipelines, dataframes, charts
chartbook ls dataframes      # List dataframes only
chartbook data get-path --pipeline <id> --dataframe <id>   # Get parquet path
chartbook data get-docs --pipeline <id> --dataframe <id>   # Print docs content
```

## Python API

```python
from chartbook import data

lf = data.load(pipeline="acme/markets", dataframe="market_data")       # through the catalog: its newest snapshot; Polars LazyFrame
df = data.load(pipeline="markets", dataframe="market_data", format="pandas")  # a bare name when only one matches
rates = data.load("fed_yield_curve:treasury_rates")                    # inside a pipeline: a dependency's pinned copy, by reference
path = data.path("my_dataframe")                                        # inside a pipeline: where its own chartbook.toml puts it

from chartbook import assets
paths = assets.files("file/filings")             # a [files] asset's files, sorted (works for a dataframe of many parts too)
table = assets.index("dep:file/filings")         # LazyFrame: path, size_bytes, sha256, a column per key=value folder; a dependency's from the store's record
docs = data.get_docs(pipeline="markets", dataframe="market_data")       # the write-up, as text
```

## Minimal Configuration Example

All `[project]` keys are optional (an empty `chartbook.toml` is a valid pipeline manifest). Project type is inferred: a `[pipelines]` registry table means catalog, otherwise pipeline. Each chart and dataframe needs exactly one of `docs_path` (external markdown file) or `docs` (inline markdown).

```toml
[project]
name = "My Pipeline"
description = "Analytics pipeline description"
maintainer = "Your Name"

[charts.my_chart]
name = "My Chart"
description = "Chart description"
dataframe = "my_data"
path = "./_output/chart.html"
docs_path = "./docs_src/charts/chart.md"

[dataframes.my_data]
name = "My Data"
description = "Data description"
sources = ["Source"]
path = "./_data/data.parquet"
date_col = "date"
docs = "Documentation for this dataset."
```

## Directory Structure

```
my-pipeline/
├── chartbook.toml      # Configuration
├── README.md           # Required; becomes the site front page
├── _data/              # Parquet data files
├── _output/            # Generated HTML charts
├── docs_src/           # Markdown documentation
│   ├── charts/
│   ├── dataframes/
│   └── site/           # Optional custom site pages
└── src/                # Python source code
```

## Catalogs and stores in 0.4.0

A catalog is `catalog.toml`, listing stores rather than working folders. `chartbook catalog migrate` keeps a backup when upgrading the old file. `chartbook catalog build` renders hubs over stored versions. `chartbook docs build` renders a pipeline site. A task runner owns the documentation step of `chartbook run`.

```console
chartbook store add NAME URL
chartbook store remove NAME
chartbook store move ID --to NAME --dry-run
chartbook ls stores
chartbook ls versions
chartbook link ID FOLDER
```

Writes follow catalog routing; reads search every store. Dependency entries may name a portable publishing URL, with anonymous S3 reads via `?anonymous=true`. Links explicitly override pins during local development, are recorded in build provenance, are ignored in CI and frozen runs, and prevent snapshots until removed.
